evidence: InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository each wrap a private Map and implement nextId, save and findById. This is storage only.
InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProjectId filters on projectId, filters.status and filters.assigneeId. This is the repository answering a query, which is persistence work.
Each class implements a domain repository interface (UserRepository, ProjectRepository, TaskRepository), which matches the role of an infrastructure adapter.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file holds in-memory adapters for the repository interfaces declared in the domain. Each class only stores entities in a Map, generates IDs and looks entities up. All of that is persistence work, which belongs in the infrastructure layer. findByProjectId applies filters for project, status and assignee, but that is just how a repository answers a query; it is not a business rule. It does not change entity state, enforce invariants or decide domain behaviour. No transport, presentation or domain-rule logic was found.
